title: Book Three · Chapter 66: The Cold Shop Door
story:
Another month passes. Winter comes with a cold wind along the lane.

On Saturday, Ronan takes a finished jacket to the fruit shop. Mrs Deng has ordered the work for her brother. He will collect it there later today.

Mum puts a note inside the bag. The work is paid for. Ronan only needs to hand it over.

At the corner, he pulls his collar up. The oranges outside the shop have a cloth over them today.

Mrs Deng is serving two customers at once. One wants apples. The other is waiting for change.

Ronan holds the door for a woman with a basket. Then he stays near the wall, out of the wind.

Mrs Deng looks up and sees the coat bag.

“One minute.”

Ronan nods. He looks at the price cards while she finishes.

The woman with the basket cannot see one card behind the fruit. She asks the price of the pears.

Ronan turns the card toward her. Mrs Deng gives the price aloud. The woman chooses four.

When the customers leave, Mrs Deng takes the jacket into the back room.

She returns with a coat over one arm.

“For your mother. My brother wants this pocket deeper.”

Ronan looks at the narrow opening. The coat feels heavier than the jacket he brought, but it fits in the same bag.

“I will tell her.”

“Can she finish it by Tuesday?”

“I don't know. She has other work. She can send you a note.”

Mrs Deng nods. “Ask her. I am only here until three today.”

Ronan writes the question on the back of Mum's note. He puts it with the coat and takes the bag home.

Mum checks the pocket herself. She turns the lining out and looks at the cloth inside.

“Wednesday,” she says. “And I need to speak to him about the size.”

She writes a short reply. Ronan takes it back while the shop is still open.

This time, Mrs Deng's brother is there. He reads the note, takes off his work gloves, and writes the size he needs.

“Wednesday is all right,” he says.

Ronan carries the answer home. His fingers are cold around the paper, so he keeps it inside his pocket.

Mum reads it at the table. Then she puts the coat on a hanger and reaches for her next piece of work.

“You can stop for today,” she tells him.

Ronan looks at the clock. The two trips took most of his morning.

He sits near the window with warm water and his school book. Outside, the fruit shop's cloth has kept the oranges out of the worst wind. Inside, his own hands slowly grow warm again.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

serve＝接待、为顾客服务；change＝找回的零钱；deeper＝更深；hanger＝衣架。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan在水果店做了哪些有限的帮助？他有没有擅自改变价格或答应交期？
2. 最后约定星期几完成？具体尺寸由谁提供、由谁确认能不能做？

## 读句子

**He puts it with the coat and takes the bag home.**

拆开看：He / puts it with the coat / and takes the bag home.

他／把写好的问题和外套放在一起／把袋子带回家。
